title: migrateIn slice ordering is a value transfer between users: emissions resume for slice 1 while later slices sit parked
description: A migration necessarily drains the pool to zero (`finalizeAndReset` requires `totalStaked == 0`) and then refills it one operator-chosen slice at a time. Emissions resume the instant slice 1 lands, but slice-N users are still in the migrator's custody earning nothing — and because the budget is shared, what slice-1 users collect is drawn from the same `rewardBudget` that funds every later user's runway. Time-in-pool, and therefore payout, is decided entirely by which slice the operator puts a user in: a variable no user controls and none can observe in advance.
impact: Value transfer between users from a shared rewardBudget. Measured 1000 bps (Alice 40.685 vs Bob 36.986 phUSD) over identical wall-clock exposure with a 3-day operational lag. At MAX_TARGET_APY (50%) and a 7-day staggered migration the transfer reaches ~0.96% of migrated notional. Protocol solvency is unaffected (asserted in PoC).
attackPath: 1. Migration necessarily drains the pool to zero (finalizeAndReset requires totalStaked == 0).
2. The operator refills it one chosen slice at a time via migrateIn.
3. Emissions resume the instant slice 1 lands.
4. Slice-N users are still in the migrator's custody earning nothing, while what slice-1 users collect is drawn from the same rewardBudget that funds every later user's runway.
5. Time-in-pool, and therefore payout, is set by slice assignment — a variable no user controls.
likelihood: certain on any multi-slice migration. Magnitude scales linearly with targetAPY and with the gap between first and last slice.
assumptions: targetAPY is non-zero during the staggered window and the migration spans more than one transaction.
justification: C4 Medium: value leak (here, redistribution) with stated assumptions and external requirements, and the function of the protocol — fair pro-rata emission from a shared budget — is impacted. Escalated from the scanner's Low under D-10 because the harmed party has ZERO agency: unlike CLASS-016 (self-advance, where a user can protect themselves with two transactions), a slice-N user cannot observe or influence their assignment. The dedup record pre-authorised a `medium` severityCeiling.
recommendation: Set targetAPY to 0 immediately after finalizeAndReset and restore it only after the final migrateIn slice lands — emissions are then zero for the whole staggered window and slice order carries no economic weight. (ECON-04 measured ~426 users/tx, so single-transaction re-injection is also viable.) Document whichever is chosen as a MANDATORY runbook step; the finding is that it is not one today.
